findings.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Exemption
findings.description: Georgia grants a homestead property tax exemption to veterans who are VA-rated 100% totally disabled, rated less than 100% but paid at the 100% rate due to individual unemployability, or who qualify for certain statutory VA awards (e.g., loss of limbs, hands, or sight). The exemption is the greater of $32,500 or the federally indexed amount under 38 U.S.C. 2102 ($121,812 for 2025, per the official state page), applied against the assessed value of the veteran's owned and occupied home for all state, county, municipal, and school ad valorem taxes.
findings.value: Exemption of the greater of $32,500 or the current 38 U.S.C. 2102 index amount ($121,812 stated for 2025) off assessed home value
otherReqs: Honorably discharged Georgia veteran (or unremarried surviving spouse / minor children of a qualified veteran)
Must own the home and occupy it as primary residence
VA-rated 100% totally disabled, OR rated less than 100% but compensated at the 100% rate due to unemployability, OR statutory VA award for loss/permanent loss of use of limbs, hands, or sight
findings.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue (filed with county tax commissioner)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Any qualifying disabled veteran who is a citizen and resident of Georgia is granted an exemption of the greater of $32,500.00 or the maximum amount which may be granted to a disabled veteran under Section 2102 of Title 38 of the United States Code, as amended, on his or her homestead which such veteran owns and actually occupies as a residence and homestead

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Ad Valorem / TAVT Vehicle Tax Exemption
findings.description: Georgia exempts one vehicle owned by a qualifying disabled veteran from ad valorem tax or Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT). Eligibility requires VA verification of 100% total and permanent service-connected disability, or unemployability at the 100% rate, or specific statutory losses (feet, hands, sight). The exemption applies to only one vehicle per veteran.
findings.value: Full ad valorem/TAVT exemption on one vehicle owned by the veteran
otherReqs: Verified by VA as 100 percent totally and permanently service-connected disabled, OR rated unemployable at the 100 percent level, OR statutory loss of feet, hands, sight, or permanent vision impairment
Exemption limited to ONLY one vehicle the veteran owns
Apply through the county tag office using Form MV-30
findings.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue (processed at county tag offices)
findings.sourceExcerpt: verified by VA to be 100 percent totally and permanently service-connected disabled ... The exemption covers ONLY one vehicle the veteran owns.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
findings.description: Georgia issues a free disabled veteran license plate for up to two motorcycles or passenger vehicles per veteran, with no registration, manufacturing, or annual fee. Eligible categories range from 100% totally and permanently disabled to certain statutory losses, and in some cases veterans compensated at less than 100% or with a nonservice-connected disability, depending on the certification path (VA entitlement letter or authorized physician statement).
findings.value: Free plate (no registration, manufacturing, or annual fee) for up to 2 motorcycles/passenger vehicles
otherReqs: Georgia resident with qualifying honorable/active-duty service

Certified by VA or an authorized physician in one of the plate's disability categories (100% permanent, 100% nonpermanent requiring annual recertification, loss/loss of use of limbs, loss of sight, or in some cases compensated at less than 100% / nonservice-connected)
findings.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Division (Special Tag Unit)
documentation: VA disabled veteran entitlement letter, OR certified statement from an authorized physician
findings.sourceExcerpt: Any disabled veteran, upon proper application, shall be allowed to receive a free disabled motor vehicle license plates for up to two motorcycles or passenger cars for personal use... There is no registration fee, manufacturing fee, or annual fee for this plate.

findings.name: Georgia War Veterans Homes (Milledgeville and Augusta)
findings.description: Georgia operates two state skilled-nursing War Veterans Homes, in Milledgeville and Augusta, for veterans who served on active duty during qualifying wartime/conflict periods, were discharged under other than dishonorable conditions, and are VA-approved as eligible for skilled nursing care. A nominal daily fee applies; for veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70% or higher, or whose admission relates to a service-connected condition, VA pays the daily fee in full.
findings.value: Nominal daily fee; fully VA-paid for veterans rated 70%+ service-connected or admitted for a service-connected condition
otherReqs: Resided in Georgia for 2 years immediately preceding application, or 5 of the past 15 years
Served on active duty during a qualifying wartime/conflict period (WWII, Post-WWII, Korea, Cold War, Vietnam, Persian Gulf)
Discharged under other than dishonorable conditions
Approved as eligible for skilled nursing care by the VA
Free of contagious infectious disease and behavioral/psychiatric problems; not sustained by line-operated mechanical means
documentation: VA eligibility determination for skilled nursing care
findings.sourceExcerpt: approved as eligible for skilled nursing care by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)... For those with service-connected disability ratings of 70% or higher, or whose admission relates to a service-connected condition, the daily fee is paid in full by VA.

findings.name: State of Georgia Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: Eligible veterans applying for State of Georgia jobs receive a bonus of 5 or 10 points added to their passing score on numerically scored pre-employment assessments; where no numerical assessment is used, equally qualified veterans receive preference over non-veteran applicants. The point-split criteria (e.g., disability-linked 10-point tier) are governed by State Personnel Board Rule 478-1-.18, which the agency's own text could not be machine-read for this research, so the exact disability threshold for the 10-point tier is not confirmed here.
findings.value: 5 or 10 points added to passing score on numerical pre-employment assessment
otherReqs: Documentation (DD-214, VA Benefit Summary Letter, etc.) submitted to the hiring agency's HR department
Preference not granted until required documentation is received
findings.agency: Georgia Department of Administrative Services (Team Georgia Careers)
documentation: VA Benefit Summary Letter (for disability-based preference)
findings.legalCitation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 478-1-.18 (State Personnel Board Rule, Veterans' Preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: a bonus of either 5 or 10 points added to their passing score on a numerical pre-employment assessment

findings.name: Georgia HERO Scholarship
findings.description: The Georgia HERO Scholarship, administered by the Georgia Student Finance Commission, provides up to $2,000 per academic year (max $8,000 over four years) to Georgia National Guard members and U.S. Military Reservists deployed to a combat zone, and to the children/spouses of such service members — including children of a service member who died or became 100% disabled from combat-zone injuries. This is not a general disabled-veteran tuition waiver; it is limited to Guard/Reserve combat deployment and its dependents.
findings.value: Up to $2,000 per academic year; maximum $8,000 over four academic years
otherReqs: Georgia residency for 12 consecutive months immediately prior to term start
Enrollment at an eligible USG, TCSG, or private nonprofit Georgia institution

Service member deployed to a combat zone 181+ cumulative days after Feb 1, 2003 (or evacuated for severe injuries), OR qualifying child/spouse of such a service member, including a child of one who died or became 100% disabled from combat-zone injuries
documentation: Proof of qualifying deployment/discharge or dependent relationship
findings.sourceExcerpt: Eligible recipients may receive up to $2,000 per academic school year... Students who meet the eligibility requirements of Categories 1, 3, or 4 may receive up to $8,000 for the equivalent of four academic years of study.

findings.name: One-Time Veterans Hunting & Fishing License
findings.description: Georgia offers a free, one-time, full-privilege sportsman's license (hunting, big game, migratory bird stamp, salt/fresh water fishing, mountain trout) to resident veterans who served 90+ days of active federal duty and were honorably discharged on or after July 1, 2005. It is valid for one year and may be issued only once; afterward, veterans may purchase a discounted lifetime license. Separately, Georgia residents certified as permanently and totally disabled (by VA, SSA, Medicaid, Medicare, or Railroad Retirement) qualify for a discounted 3-year disability sportsman's license.
findings.value: Free one-time, one-year full-privilege license; discounted 3-year disability sportsman's license for permanently/totally disabled residents
otherReqs: Georgia resident veteran with 90+ days active Federal duty, honorably discharged July 1, 2005 or later (one-time license)
For the disability sportsman's license: certified permanently and totally disabled by VA, SSA, Medicaid, Medicare, or Railroad Retirement
DD Form 214 copy and current Georgia driver's license/ID required for the one-time veterans license
findings.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
documentation: Georgia driver's license or ID card
VA/SSA/Medicaid/Medicare/Railroad Retirement disability certification (for disability license)
findings.sourceExcerpt: A One Time Veterans License is available free to Georgia resident military veterans who served on active Federal duty for 90 or more days and were honorably discharged on July 1, 2005 or later... valid for one year from date of issue... may be issued only once.

findings.name: Free Veteran Designation on Georgia Driver's License/ID
findings.description: Georgia resident veterans who served on active duty and received an honorable or medical discharge (or National Guard members with 20 years of service) can receive a free veteran designation on their Georgia driver's license or ID card. Activation for training purposes only does not qualify.
findings.value: Free veteran designation added to driver's license/ID (no fee stated for the designation itself)
otherReqs: Honorable or medical discharge (or 20 years National Guard service)
Current Georgia resident
Activation for training purposes only does not qualify
documentation: DD Form 214 (Member 4 copy) or GDVS-endorsed Certificate of Eligibility
findings.sourceExcerpt: Only veterans with an honorable discharge or a medical discharge are entitled to a free veteran driver's license... Activation for training purposes does not qualify for a veteran driver's license.
